title: The Afternoon Brief: Cutdown day's fallout meets a Grand Slam upset
dek: NFL rosters settled into shape after Sunday's 6 p.m. deadline, with two off-field cases still open, while Djokovic's first-round exit reshaped the US Open draw.
author: GoCheckMySports
key_fact: The NFL's cutdown weekend produced routine roster churn alongside two unresolved disciplinary matters, Josh Jacobs and Keenan Allen, that now sit with the league and the courts rather than any team's depth chart.
bottom_line: Sunday's NFL cutdown deadline produced ordinary roster business, the Bears-Falcons Dexter trade, the Bills-Colts Van Pran-Granger deal, Beckham making the Giants' roster, and Aaron Donald ending his retirement with the Rams, alongside two unresolved off-field matters in Keenan Allen's DWI arrest and Josh Jacobs' placement on the commissioner's exempt list. The honest read is that the reporting establishes what happened in each case clearly but does not yet show what either team or the league will decide next. In tennis, Djokovic's first-round loss to world No. 49 Mariano Navone, his first opening-round Grand Slam exit since 2006, reshaped a US Open draw already missing Jannik Sinner. Coming checkpoints include the three-day appeal window on Jacobs' exempt-list placement, any update on Allen's legal process, Ohtani's next pitching target date, and how far Alcaraz and the leading women's contenders advance at Flushing Meadows.
body: The through-line today is a league moving on two tracks at once. On one track, cutdown day did what cutdown day does: teams reshuffled rosters through trades, waiver claims, and returns from absence. On the other, two Sunday incidents involving Colts receiver Keenan Allen and Packers running back Josh Jacobs turned the same 53-man deadline into a story about legal exposure and league process that has not resolved.

The roster moves themselves were straightforward business. The Bears traded 2023 second-round pick Gervon Dexter to the Falcons for cornerback Clark Phillips and a fifth-round pick ahead of the deadline. The Bills sent center Sedrick Van Pran-Granger to the Colts for a 2027 sixth-round pick, giving up a 2027 seventh-round pick in return. The Giants kept Odell Beckham Jr. on their initial 53-man roster after he missed all of 2025, and Aaron Donald ended a two-year retirement to sign a one-year, $20 million deal with the Rams, pairing with Myles Garrett ahead of the Rams' opener. All 32 teams faced the same 6 p.m. ET Sunday deadline to reach 53 players, per the day's roster tracker.

The more serious threads are unresolved. Keenan Allen, 34, was arrested early Sunday in downtown Indianapolis on preliminary charges of DWI and DWI endangering a person, both misdemeanors, with a blood alcohol content measured at 0.08 or more, hours after his preseason debut against Detroit. Separately, Josh Jacobs was placed on the NFL's commissioner's exempt list on August 30, barring him from practicing, attending games, or playing while he faces misdemeanor charges of battery and criminal damage to property announced by the Brown County District Attorney's Office on August 28. Jacobs will be paid while on the list, and he and the NFLPA have three days after formal notification to appeal.

In baseball, the day carried a mix of milestones and roster churn rather than crisis. Max Scherzer struck out 10 against the Mariners to reach 3,535 career strikeouts, passing Gaylord Perry for ninth all-time. Pete Crow-Armstrong hit three home runs in the Cubs' 17-5 win over the Reds, sharpening his NL MVP case against Shohei Ohtani, who was held out of a scheduled Sunday start as his return timeline as a pitcher remains unclear per manager Dave Roberts. The Red Sox activated Roman Anthony and Trevor Story from the injured list after absences of more than three months apiece. The Cardinals placed rookie second baseman JJ Wetherholt, an NL Rookie of the Year candidate, on the injured list with right wrist tendinitis after he played through discomfort for weeks. The Orioles claimed outfielder Luis Robert Jr. off waivers from the Mets on Monday as part of their September roster positioning.

At the US Open, Novak Djokovic lost to world No. 49 Mariano Navone 7-6 (7-5) 5-7 4-6 6-2 6-1 in the first round on August 31, his first opening-round exit at Flushing Meadows and his first Grand Slam first-round loss since 2006. Djokovic said afterward he has been dealing with health issues "pretty much every match this year." The tournament's shape shifted further with world No. 1 Jannik Sinner absent through injury and defending champion Carlos Alcaraz returning from a wrist injury. Aryna Sabalenka opened her title defense with a 6-2, 6-4 win over Camila Osorio, beginning a bid for a third consecutive title, while Venus Williams lost to Sofia Kenin, extending her losing streak in singles.

The reporting does not explain why Wetherholt played through wrist discomfort for weeks before the IL placement, nor does it specify a revised return timeline for Ohtani beyond the team's stated expectation that he pitches again this season. On the Allen and Jacobs matters, the inputs describe the arrest, the charges, and the league's exempt-list mechanism, but do not state what roster or disciplinary action either club or the league will take next; that remains open.
Desk boards were not available for this edition, so today's numbers come entirely from the day's reporting rather than a league feed.

The checkpoints ahead are concrete. The appeal window on Jacobs' exempt-list placement runs three days from his formal notification. Allen's case proceeds through the Indianapolis Metro Police Department's charges, with the Colts' roster status and any NFL Personal Conduct Policy review still pending. Ohtani's next pitching target date has not been set. Donald's availability for the Rams' season-opening trip to Melbourne remains unconfirmed. At the US Open, the men's draw now turns on Alcaraz's health through the rounds, and the women's No. 1 ranking depends on how far Sabalenka, Elena Rybakina, Coco Gauff, and Jessica Pegula advance.
